benefits: Finds the GCD of up to 8 numbers instantly - no long division by hand.
Lists every common factor, not just the greatest one.
Exact BigInt arithmetic: no rounding, even for huge integers.
The coprime check tells you at a glance when numbers share nothing but 1.

faqs.a: The GCD (greatest common divisor) is the largest number that divides all of them exactly. For 12, 18, 24 it is 6, because 6 divides each one and no larger number does.
Numbers are coprime when their GCD is 1 - they share no factor besides 1. 7 and 11 are coprime. The tool tells you this directly.
List the factors of the smallest number and test each against the rest - or let this tool do it: the common factors of 12, 18, 24 are 1, 2, 3, 6.
faqs.q: How do I find common factors by hand?

faqs.a: Yes - negatives are converted to their absolute values first, since factors are about divisibility. -12 and 18 have GCD 6.
The GCD is still computed and shown, but the full factor list is skipped past one trillion to keep the page fast. The GCD alone answers most real questions.
faqs.q: Why is the factor list missing for huge numbers?

faqs.a: Fractions have infinitely many common divisors, so the idea only makes sense for whole numbers. Non-integers are ignored by this tool.

common-factor-calculator.formula:
Euclid's algorithm: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b), until the remainder is 0.
Example: gcd(18, 12): 18 mod 12 = 6; 12 mod 6 = 0 -> gcd = 6.
For more numbers: gcd(a, b, c) = gcd(gcd(a, b), c).
Common factors = all divisors of the GCD.
howTo: Type 2 to 8 whole numbers, separated by commas, spaces, or new lines.
The greatest common divisor appears instantly as the headline result.
Below it you get every common factor, smallest to largest.
A note appears when your numbers are coprime (GCD = 1).
keyFacts: A common factor divides every number in the list with no remainder.
Common factors of 12, 18, 24 are 1, 2, 3, 6 - every divisor of the GCD.
Numbers with GCD 1 are called coprime (example: 7 and 11).
The GCD never exceeds the smallest number in the list.
Negative inputs are treated by absolute value; non-integers are skipped.

common-factor-calculator.workedExample:
Numbers: 12, 18, 24
1. gcd(12, 18): 18 mod 12 = 6; 12 mod 6 = 0 -> 6.
2. gcd(6, 24): 24 mod 6 = 0 -> 6.
3. GCD = 6.
4. Divisors of 6: 1, 2, 3, 6 - these are all the common factors.
